In ERCOT, interconnecting generation customers pay a limited interconnection cost to cover certain direct costs of connecting to the transmission system, and the remaining costs are passed to customers based on usage (Wilson et al. 2024). 3. Usage-based methods are the most common approach for regional cost allocation. Outside of local8 and generator interconnection projects, most regions and project types use some type of usage-based method to allocate costs. The most common usage-based approach is a postage stamp method that uses electricity load as a proxy for usage. Some regions, such as SPP, combine usage-based methods with other methods, such as license plate allocation, to limit the usage-based cost responsibility to specific subregions or zones. While usage-based allocation is primarily based on load ratio share in most regions, PJM also uses power flow modeling to approximate network usage. 4. Direct cost allocation based on quantified benefits or costs is rarely used. Most regions use network usage as a proxy for benefits rather than allocating costs based on quantified benefits or costs. MISO and the NYISO use estimated benefits to allocate costs among load zones for economic projects, which account for a small share of total transmission investments. Within each load zone a usage-based approach is then used to allocate costs. PJM’s framework uses a cost-causer approach for its multi-driver projects that meet multiple needs such as reliability or economic or public policy. Costs for this project type, which has not been utilized to date, would be allocated by dividing the project costs between the individual drivers (i.e., reliability, economic) and assigning costs using the method developed for the project type under that driver. 5. Even when regions use the same method, it is often implemented differently. Regions have developed different approaches for implementing their cost allocation methods, reflecting regional preferences and system conditions. For example, each of the seven regions has some form of postage stamp method that allocates costs in proportion to electricity load, but no two regions use the same method to calculate this “load ratio share” (Table 4). 8 Note that many local transmission charges are based on usage by local load.
